explore-widths.title: Compare the modes
explore-widths.prompt: Switch modes and find the widest signal.
hints: Try each of the three modes.
explore-widths.success: FM voice is widest, about 16 kHz. SSB is about 2.4 kHz and CW about 150 Hz.

explore-ssb-filter.title: Choose a filter for SSB
explore-ssb-filter.prompt: Choose the filter that passes the whole SSB signal without letting in lots of extra noise.
hints: At 250 Hz most of the voice is cut off.
Match the filter to the signal's width, about 2.4 kHz.
explore-ssb-filter.success: 2.4 kHz passes the whole voice signal. Narrower loses information; 6 kHz lets in extra noise.

explore-cw-qrm.title: CW with interference
explore-cw-qrm.prompt: Choose a filter that keeps your CW station and shuts out the one 300 Hz away.
hints: 500 Hz still lets part of it in.
explore-cw-qrm.success: 250 Hz: your station fits and the interference falls outside the filter.

explore-tune.title: Tune in the SSB station
explore-tune.prompt: Tune until the voice sounds natural: within 100 Hz.
hints: Bring the tuning offset toward 0 Hz.
explore-tune.success: Within 100 Hz the voice sounds right. SSB is the mode that needs accurate tuning.

explore-agc.title: Fading signals
explore-agc.prompt: Turn on AGC to stop the volume jumping as the signal fades.
explore-agc.success: With AGC on, a 60 dB fade becomes a 3 dB wobble in volume.
